reasoning: iter-032: simd_exp_f32x4_fast (degree-4 Maclaurin) for the blend SIMD hot path. Hypothesis: each (g, mb) pair calls simd_exp 8x, so shaving 1 FMA per call = 8 ops saved per pair * 65k pairs = ~520k SIMD ops saved per frame; on 10 cores @ 4 SIMD FMA / cycle * 4 GHz this is sub-microsecond, but the compounding effect across all stages might matter. Result: blend p50 5.30 ms unchanged (vs 5.28 ms iter-031); sum 156.6 ms vs 157.7 ms = 0.7% noise. Macro sum_total_ms 341.2 -> 340.2 ms (well inside trial-to-trial std). PSNR min 60.33 -> 60.34 (off bit-identity by 5e-5 alpha as expected). Conclusion: blend is NOT compute-bound on Apple Silicon NEON; the per-(g,mb) loop is memory-bound on the random gauss_rec / colors fetches. Saving 1 FMA per exp does not move the needle. Reverting to keep bit-identity with iter-031 and avoid degree-4 maintenance burden until we have a profiler-proven blend-FPU bottleneck. Next direction: attack the random-access memory pattern (e.g. pack colors into gauss_rec; tile-local AoS gather; cross-tile microblock LPT) rather than further FPU micro-opts.
